kind: protected prompt native guard remediation evidence
summary: The prior protected prompt failure was traced to Codex app-server native execution. Runtime config now enables OpenClaw sandboxing for all sessions, pins exec away from gateway-native execution, and sets the Codex plugin to guardian mode. The installed guard blocks native bash and direct app-server execution methods for the active main session.
commands: docker exec openclaw-gateway openclaw config validate --json
docker exec openclaw-gateway openclaw sandbox explain --agent main --json
node import @openclaw/codex/dist/sandbox-guard and evaluate native execution blocks
grep marker P5_PROTECTED_PROMPT_TEST_AFTER_NATIVE_GUARD in OpenClaw session traces

cases.name: native bash surface
cases.result: Codex-native bash is unavailable because OpenClaw sandboxing is active for this session. This mode cannot route execution through the OpenClaw sandbox backend. Use a normal Codex harness turn, or run an intentionally unsandboxed session.

cases.name: app-server turn/start direct method
cases.result: Codex-native app-server method `turn/start` is unavailable because OpenClaw exec host=node is active for this session. OpenClaw exec host=node is active for this session. Codex app-server native execution cannot route shell, filesystem, MCP, or app-backed work through the selected OpenClaw node. Use a normal Codex harness turn so OpenClaw exec/process tools run on the node, or switch exec host to gateway for native Codex app-server execution.

cases.name: app-server command/exec direct method
cases.result: Codex-native app-server method `command/exec` is unavailable because OpenClaw exec host=node is active for this session. OpenClaw exec host=node is active for this session. Codex app-server native execution cannot route shell, filesystem, MCP, or app-backed work through the selected OpenClaw node. Use a normal Codex harness turn so OpenClaw exec/process tools run on the node, or switch exec host to gateway for native Codex app-server execution.

limitations: A direct model-driven protected-prompt drill after the guard change hit the local command timeout before a clean JSON response was returned.
No post-guard marker was found in session traces and no openclaw agent process remained active after the timeout.
P5 should remain active until a clean owner-mobile protected-action drill returns a terminal denial or approval packet and Control UI/mobile state alignment is captured.
